summary: InteractiveAppHost exposes no surface-changed notification, so a product cannot re-fit its logical canvas after a runtime window-mode change. Its seven members (Init/Update/View/MapKey/MapPointer/Tick/MapKeyChord) are all either coordinate-free or receive the LOGICAL size; CaptureOutputSize and InitialOutputSize belong to the bounded-run evidence workflow (ViewerRunEffect / ViewerRunEvidence), not to an interactive host. This makes the reported Borderless defect structurally unfixable in product code.
cost: none - established before writing code, which is what kept the cycle from attempting a product-side re-fit the contract forbids.

summary: Effect-emission coverage certified a shipped setting that bricked the UI. BehaviorTests already looped all three display modes asserting each emits ApplyWindowOptions and ApplyLogicalCanvas, and every one of those assertions was TRUE the whole time Borderless was unusable - the effect wiring was never the fault. An emission assertion cannot distinguish a window request that works from one that leaves every button dead, so a green suite reported coverage of exactly the surface that was broken.
evidence: file:tests/Rogue3.Tests/BehaviorTests.fs:417-440 (the pre-existing per-mode emission loop, unchanged and still passing);issue:EHotwagner/rogue3#63 comment 2 (a test that asserts ApplyLogicalCanvas was emitted with the right Size would pass today and must not be accepted as coverage)
cost: none for this cycle - the issue had already diagnosed it; the cost was borne by the players who hit the trap and by the cycles that shipped past it.
owner: EHotwagner/rogue3 - tests; and FS-GG/FS.GG.Rendering fs-gg-testing, which could name emission-only host-effect assertions as a known-insufficient evidence class.

summary: Pairing a fit-sensitive acceptance assertion with an explicit NEGATIVE CONTROL is what gave the regression test teeth. The acceptance clicks a button at its real on-screen point inverted through the POST-change surface fit; the control re-inverts the SAME physical sample through two stale surfaces and asserts both miss. Re-pointing only the acceptance click at the stale surface fails the test, which proves the assertion is about WHICH surface the fit was taken against and not merely about the click landing somewhere.
evidence: command:dotnet test Rogue3.slnx -c Release --no-build (274 passed at branch head; 273 passed / 1 failed for each of three single-edit mutants: restoring Borderless->WindowedFullscreen in windowBehavior, re-adding Borderless to shellConfig.DisplayModes, and swapping the acceptance click onto preChangeSurface);file:tests/Rogue3.Tests/BehaviorTests.fs (the #63 test)
owner: FS-GG/FS.GG.Rendering - fs-gg-testing could carry this as a named pattern: any test asserting a coordinate route should state the stale input it would reject.

summary: The native window tier was available in this environment and proved the mitigation at the boundary no pure seam can reach. Extending the existing capability-gated #1022 test to drive BOTH Fullscreen and Borderless through a real bounded window run observes the framework reporting 'Runtime window behavior applied: mode=fullscreen' for both - so the remap is confirmed by what the compositor was actually asked for, not only by what the product emitted. This repository's completion report records native play as its standing coverage gap, and this is the first cycle to close part of it.
evidence: command:dotnet test Rogue3.slnx -c Release --no-build (274 passed, Skipped: 0 - the T2 gate did not trip);command:the same run with the asserted diagnostic string replaced by an unmatchable probe, which failed in 487 ms and confirms the test executes rather than silently skipping;file:tests/Rogue3.Tests/BehaviorTests.fs (the #1022/#63 native test)
cost: none - one extra bounded two-frame window run, reusing the existing gated test rather than adding a second launch path.
owner: EHotwagner/rogue3 - tests; the reusable point is that a capability-gated native test should be teeth-checked with an unmatchable assertion, because a skipped gate and a passing test are indistinguishable in the summary line.
